:::info

Die Dokumentation dieser Integration wird von ihrem Autor geschrieben und ist bisher nur auf Englisch verfügbar.

This integration drives **Onkyo network AV receivers** from Gladys, as well as
the **Integra** and recent **Pioneer** models that speak the same protocol
(eISCP).

Everything stays **local**: Gladys talks to the receiver directly on your
network (port 60128). No account, no cloud, no Internet.

## Before you start

1. The receiver must be **on the network** (cable or Wi-Fi).
2. Turn on **Network Standby** on the receiver: `Setup` → `Hardware` →
   `Power Management` → `Network Standby` → `On` (the wording varies a little
   between models). Without it the receiver drops the network in standby: Gladys
   loses it and cannot switch it on.
3. Give it a **fixed IP** in your router (recommended, not required: if the IP
   changes, the integration finds the receiver again by its MAC address).

Some older models accept one connection at a time: if the Onkyo Remote app is
open, the receiver may refuse Gladys. Close the app and wait a minute.

## Adding a receiver

1. Install the integration from the Gladys store.
2. Open the **Discovery** tab: Gladys looks for receivers on the network.
3. Add the one(s) that show up. One device is created per **zone**.

The receiver does not show up? It may sit on another subnet or a VLAN: type its
IP in **Receiver addresses** (several separated by commas), save, then run the
discovery again.

## Settings

| Setting                          | What it does                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Receiver addresses**           | Only for a receiver the discovery does not find. E.g. `192.168.1.40, 192.168.1.41`                                                                           |
| **Zones**                        | `Automatic`: the zones the receiver declares (the main zone alone on older models). Or force 1, 2 or 3 zones.                                                |
| **Volume scale of the receiver** | The highest volume value the receiver shows: 80 on most models, 200 on recent ones that step by 0.5. "Test the connection" tells what the receiver declares. |
| **Maximum volume (%)**           | Gladys **never** sends a volume above it, whatever a slider, a button or a scene asks. 80 % by default.                                                      |
| **Detailed logs**                | Logs every message exchanged with the receiver. Turn it on to understand a problem, then off again.                                                          |

The volume is a **percentage of the scale**: 50 % on a scale of 80 shows 40 on
the receiver.

## What you get

### Main zone

- **Power** (on / standby)
- **Volume** (slider, in %), **Volume up**, **Volume down**, **Mute** (toggle)
- **Input**: the list of inputs, with the names you gave them on the receiver
  (recent models) or the standard names (BD/DVD, CD, NET…)
- **Listening mode**: Stereo, Direct, Dolby, DTS…
- **Tuner preset** (1 to 40)
- **Play, Pause, Stop, Previous, Next**: for the network, USB or Bluetooth player
  of the receiver
- **Now playing**: artist and title

### Zone 2 and zone 3

Power, volume, mute, volume up/down, input. The "Main zone source" input makes
the zone follow the main one.

Every change made **on the remote, the front panel or another app** shows up in
Gladys at once: the receiver reports it, Gladys does not need to poll.

## Scenes (Gladys 5.1+)

### Triggers

- **The input of a receiver changed**: someone picked another input (remote,
  front panel, app). Filter by zone and by input. Variables: `source` (code) and
  `source_name` (name). Gladys' own orders never fire it (no loop).
- **A new track is playing**: the network or USB player moved to another track.
  Variables: `title`, `artist`, `album`.
- **A receiver went online or offline**: the link dropped (unplugged, network
  standby off) or came back. A restart of Gladys never fires it.

### Actions

- **Play an input on a receiver**: switches the zone on if needed, waits for it,
  picks the input, then sets the volume (optional). Made for "the radio in the
  kitchen at 7:00".
- **Mute a receiver**: mute, unmute or toggle.
- **Set the listening mode** of the main zone.
- **Send an ISCP command**: any command of the Onkyo protocol, for what the other
  actions do not cover. The receiver's answer is available to the next actions.

Example: "when the TV switches on → Play the TV input at 35 %".

## Dashboard widget (Gladys 5.1+)

The **Onkyo receiver** widget shows one zone (picked in its settings, or the
first receiver's main zone):

- volume and input;
- status: power, track playing, sound, listening mode, link;
- buttons: on/standby, volume down, volume up, mute.

## Configuration buttons

- **Test the connection**: one line per zone (connected or not, power, input,
  volume) and the typed addresses that answered nothing.
- **Send an ISCP command**: try a command before putting it in a scene.
  Examples: `PWR01` (on), `MVL20` (volume), `SLI23` (CD input), `LMDQSTN` (which
  listening mode?).

## Troubleshooting

| Problem                                   | Hint                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The receiver is not in Discovery          | Network standby on? Same network as Gladys? Otherwise type its IP in "Receiver addresses".                     |
| "Unreachable" as soon as it is in standby | Turn on network standby (see above).                                                                           |
| The volume does not match the display     | Set "Volume scale of the receiver" (80 or 200 most of the time).                                               |
| An input is missing from the list         | Older models do not announce their inputs: the standard list is used. Use "Send an ISCP command" with `SLIxx`. |
| Play/Pause do nothing                     | These keys drive the receiver's own network/USB/Bluetooth player, not an HDMI source.                          |

For a bug report, turn on **Detailed logs**, reproduce the problem and attach the
logs **without** IP or MAC addresses:
[https://github.com/prohand/gladys-onkyo/issues](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-onkyo/issues)

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Onkyo in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | Nein | The receivers are found on your network: open the Discovery tab and add them. Everything stays local (eISCP protocol, port 60128), no account, no cloud. On the receiver, turn on Network Standby (Setup > Hardware > Power Management), or Gladys loses it as soon as it goes to standby. |
| Receiver addresses | `string` | Nein | Only for a receiver the Discovery tab does not find (another subnet, a VLAN): its IP address, several separated by commas. A fixed IP in your router is recommended. |
| Zones | `select` | Nein | One Gladys device per zone. Automatic: the zones the receiver declares (the main zone alone on older models). |
| Volume scale of the receiver | `select` | Nein | The highest volume value the receiver shows. 80 on most models, 200 on recent ones that step by 0.5. "Test the connection" tells what the receiver declares. |
| Maximum volume (%) | `number` | Nein | Gladys never sends a volume above this, whatever a scene or a slider asks: protects your speakers and your ears. |
| Detailed logs (debug) | `boolean` | Nein | Log every message exchanged with the receivers. Turn it on to understand a problem, then off again: it is verbose. |

## So installierst du Onkyo in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Onkyo erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-onkyo:1.0.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-onkyo](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-onkyo).

Onkyo benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Onkyo ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [prohand](https://github.com/prohand) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
